Rashi on Keritot 11b:12:1.hebrew: ר"מ היא - דאמר אם הביאוהו שנים כו':
Rashi on Keritot 11b:12:1.english: [It] is Rabbi Meir - Who says: "If two [witnesses] brought him," etc.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:13:1.english: What does it teach us? Behold, we learn it from the latter clause - For [the Mishnah] teaches: "Two [witnesses] say: He ate, etc."

Rashi on Keritot 11b:13:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר סיפא דבר זה - ששנינו למעלה, אמרו לו אכלת כו' מביא חטאת, לאו דברי הכל היא, אלא מחלוקת ר"מ וחכמים, שרבי מאיר אומר אם הביאוהו שנים כו', וחכמים אומרים כו'. וסיפא מפרש לרישא:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:13:2.english: This is what the latter clause is saying: "This matter" - [that] which we learned above, "[If witnesses] said to him: You ate [forbidden fat], etc., he brings a sin offering," is not the opinion of everyone; rather, [it is] a dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages, as Rabbi Meir says, "If two [witnesses] brought him [to liability], etc.," and the Sages say, etc. And the latter clause explains the first clause.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:14:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי - הכי פריך הש"ס: אמרו משמע חד כו':
Rashi on Keritot 11b:14:1.english: There are those who say - This is how the Talmud raises the difficulty: "They said" implies [even] one [witness], etc.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:15:1.hebrew: מותרת לחזור לו - לראשון. ועל פי עדים, שאמרו לה שנים: "מת בעליך", ולפיכך מותרת לראשון, שהרי אנוסה היא ששנים אמרו לה, דאונס בישראל שרי:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:15:1.english: She is permitted to return to him - To the first [husband]. And [she had remarried] on the basis of witnesses, where two [witnesses] told her, "Your husband died," and therefore she is permitted to the first [husband], for she is [considered] coerced since two [witnesses] told her, as [a case of] coercion is permitted for an Israelite [husband].

Rashi on Keritot 11b:16:1.hebrew: מכלל דרישא - דקתני תצא מזה ומזה, שנשאת ברשות ב"ד ועד אחד, דהוה לה למידק יפה אם מת. דהאי דשריוה רבנן לאנסובי על פי עד אחד, משום דדייקא ומנסבא — דמתוך חומר שהחמרת עליה בסופה דתצא מזה ומזה, הקלת עליה בתחלתה, כדאמר במסכת יבמות (דף פח.). ואמטו להכי, נשאת על פי עד אחד והיא גופה לא דייקא ואישתכח דלא מת, תצא מזה ומזה, כדאמרינן במסכת סוטה (דף כז:): "ונטמאה" "ונטמאה" שני פעמים — אחד לבעל ואחד לבועל:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:16:1.english: By inference, [one may conclude] that the first clause - Which teaches [that] "she must leave this one and that one" [refers to a case] where she married with the consent of the court and [on the testimony of] one witness, for she should have investigated thoroughly whether [her husband] died. For the reason the Rabbis permitted her to marry on the basis of one witness is because she investigates [thoroughly] before marrying — for because of the stringency that you imposed upon her at the end, that "she must leave this one and that one," you were lenient with her at the beginning, as is stated in Tractate Yevamot (88a). Therefore, [if] she married on the basis of one witness and she herself did not investigate [thoroughly], and it turns out that he did not die, she must leave this one and that one, as we say in Tractate Sotah (27b): "[And she] is defiled," "[and she] is defiled" — two times, one for the husband and one for the paramour.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:19:1.hebrew: לעולם דלא מכחיש ליה - ומתניתין הכי קתני: אמרו לו [כו'], בד"א — בשותק; אבל מכחישו, כגון עד אמר אכל והוא אמר לא אכלתי — פטור:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:19:1.english: Actually, [it is] where he does not contradict him - And the Mishnah teaches thus: "[If] they said to him" [etc.] — in what case are these words said? Where he is silent; but [if] he contradicts him — for example, a witness said, "He ate," and he said, "I did not eat" — he is exempt.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:20:1.english: Is known to him - [This] implies [that he became aware] on his own, and not that others inform him.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:4:1.hebrew: נמצא מתכוין ומערה בשפחה - שהערה בה בכוונה פטור, דהעראה בשפחה פטור כשאינו מתכוין דעריות. העראה פלוגתא היא (בסנהדרין בארבע מיתות) (סנהדרין דף נה:): איכא למ"ד העראה זו נשיקה, ואיכא למאן דאמר זו הכנסת עטרה:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:4:1.english: It has been determined [that] one who [acts] intentionally and engages in the initial stage of intercourse with a maidservant - [meaning] that [if] he engaged in the initial stage of intercourse with her intentionally, he is exempt, for the initial stage of intercourse with a maidservant is exempt, like one who [engages in intercourse] unintentionally with forbidden relatives. [The definition of] the initial stage of intercourse [ha'arah] is a dispute (in Sanhedrin, in [the chapter] Arba Mitot) (Sanhedrin 55b): there is one who says ha'arah is contact [without penetration], and there is one who says it is the insertion of the corona.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:6:1.english: They said to him - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:7:1.english: If they brought him, etc. - For example, if they testified against him that he killed a person.

Rashi on Keritot 11b:7:2.hebrew: אם ירצה לומר מזיד הייתי - אם היה רוצה לפטור עצמו בשקר, היה יכול לומר מזיד היה, ומזיד פטור:
Rashi on Keritot 11b:7:2.english: If he wishes to say, "I acted intentionally" - If he wanted to exempt himself with a lie, he could have said he acted intentionally, and an intentional transgressor is exempt [from bringing an offering].

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:11:1.hebrew: אימא מציעתא עד אומר אכל והוא אומר לא אכלתי כו' - והוא הדין דמצי מייתי מרישא: "עד אומר אכל ועד אומר לא אכל", ומביא אשם תלוי; טעמא דאמר עד אחד "לא אכל", הא לאו הכי — חייב חטאת, דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא. דע"כ מיירי דשתק, דאי מכחיש ליה — פטור לגמרי, ואפילו אומר "איני יודע", כמו שפירשתי:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:11:1.english: Say the middle clause: A witness says he ate, and he says: I did not eat, etc. - And the same is true that [the Gemara] could have brought [its proof] from the first clause: "One witness says he ate, and one witness says he did not eat," and he brings a provisional guilt-offering; the reason is that one witness said "he did not eat," [implying that] were it not so, he would be liable for a sin-offering, because silence is like an admission. For perforce [the Mishnah] is speaking of [a case] where he was silent, since if he contradicts him, he is completely exempt — and even if he says "I do not know," as I explained.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:12:1.hebrew: אלא דקא מכחיש להו ומני ר"מ היא - דליכא למימר דמיירי כשאמר "איני יודע", דפשיטא דחייב, ד"איני יודע" גבי תרי עדים הויא כשתיקה:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:12:1.english: "Rather, [it is a case] where he contradicts them, and whose [opinion] is it? It is Rabbi Meir's" - For one cannot say that it is dealing with [a case] where he said, "I do not know," because it is obvious that he is liable, since [saying] "I do not know" with regard to two witnesses is like silence.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:2:1.hebrew: הכי קתני עשו כו' - והכי פירוש דברייתא: עשו גומר כמערה ומתכוון כשאינו מתכוון, והאי דינא הוי בכדרכה ושלא כדרכה, כדמפרש הש"ס. ומכל מקום קצת קשה: אמאי לא תנא "ניעור כישן" בהדייהו, ותנא ליה בתריה ד"כדרכה ושלא כדרכה":
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:2:1.english: "This is what it is teaching: They rendered, etc." - And this is the explanation of the baraita: "They rendered one who completes [intercourse] like one who engages in the initial stage, and one who has intention like one who does not have intention," and this law applies to "[intercourse] in the typical manner and in an atypical manner," as the Talmud explains. Nevertheless, it is somewhat difficult: why did [the baraita] not teach "one who is awake like one who is sleeping" together with them, and [instead] taught it after "[intercourse] in the typical manner and in an atypical manner"?

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:4:1.hebrew: נמצא מתכוין כו' - קשה, אמאי האריך הש"ס בלישניה? דהאי לאו פירוש דברייתא הוא, דכבר אסיקנא ליה שפיר:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:4:1.english: "It has been determined [that] one who [engages in intercourse] intentionally, etc." - It is difficult: why did the Talmud lengthen its phrasing [here]? For this is not an explanation of the baraita, as we have already concluded it well.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:4:2.hebrew: כשאין מתכוין דעריות - פירש הקונטרס: כגון שאשתו ואחותו במטה וכסבור לבא על אשתו ונמצא אחותו, דפטור ממלקות וחייב חטאת הואיל ונהנה, דמתעסק הוא. וקשה: שהרי בשפחה נמי חייב חטאת בכי האי גוונא, שהרי מביאין על הזדון כשוגג! וא"כ, מאי קאמר: "נמצא מתכוין בשפחה כשאין מתכוין לעריות"? בכה"ג שוו תרווייהו! לכך יש לומר: כשאין מתכוין דעריות — כגון נפל מן הגג ונתקע, דפטור לגמרי דאנוס הוא:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:4:2.english: Like one who does not intend with forbidden relations - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained [that this refers to a case] such as where his wife and his sister are in bed, and he intends to have intercourse with his wife and it turns out [to be] his sister, where he is exempt from lashes and liable [to bring] a sin-offering since he derived pleasure, for he is [considered] one who acts unawares [mit'asek]. And this is difficult, for in [the case of] a maidservant too, he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering in such a case, since one brings [an offering] for an intentional [act] just as for an unwitting [act]! And if so, what does [the Gemara] mean [when it says]: "It has been determined that one who intends with a maidservant is like one who does not intend with forbidden relations"? In such a case, both of them are equal! Therefore, one must say [that] "like one who does not intend with forbidden relations" [refers to a case] such as where he fell from the roof and became inserted, where he is completely exempt because he is coerced:

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:1.hebrew: אמרו לו עד אומר לו אכל כו' - צ"ל דמיירי שהעידוהו שנים בבת אחת, דאי בזה אחר זה — הא כ"מ שהאמינה תורה עד אחד, הרי כאן שנים, וכיון שנתקבל עדותו, תו לא קפדינן בעדות השני שאומר "לא אכל". וצ"ל דמיירי שהאיש שמעידין בו שותק, דאי אמר "איני יודע" — פטור, כדנפקא בגמרא: "או הודע אליו" כו'; ומסיק דמיירי בעד אחד שאינו יכול לחייבו קרבן, וע"כ מיירי שאותו שהעיד עליו אומר "איני יודע", דאי אמר "לא אכלתי" — פשיטא דעד אחד לא מהימן, כדכתיב (דברים יט): "לא יקום עד אחד באיש", דנראה שאין עד אחד קם רק לשבועה:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:1.english: "They said to him; a witness says to him: He ate," etc. - One must say that [the Mishnah] is speaking of a case where two [witnesses] testified against him simultaneously, for if [they testified] one after the other — behold, wherever the Torah believed one witness, it is as if there are two [witnesses] here, and once his testimony was accepted, we no longer care about the testimony of the second [witness] who says, "He did not eat." And one must say that it is speaking of a case where the person against whom they testify is silent, for if he said, "I do not know," he is exempt, as is derived in the Gemara [from the verse]: "If [his sin] be made known to him," etc.; and [the Gemara] concludes that it is speaking of a single witness, who cannot obligate him [to bring] an offering, and perforce it is speaking of a case where the one against whom he testified says, "I do not know," for if he said, "I did not eat," it is obvious that a single witness is not believed, as it is written (Deuteronomy 19[:15]): "One witness shall not rise up against a man," from which it appears that a single witness rises up only for an oath.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:2.hebrew: ואשה אומרת לא אכל - מכאן משמע דאשה מהימנא טפי מגזלן, שהרי גבי גזלן משמע דלא אמרי' שתיקה כהודאה, כדאמרינן (קדושין דף סו.): "אי מהימנא לך דלא גזלנא הוא זיל אפקה", ואע"ג דשתקה; אלמא לא אמרינן שתיקה כהודאה דמיא. ועובדא הוה: ההוא סמיא דהוה מסדר מתנייתא קמי דרב ששת כו', אתא חד גברא ואמר שאשתו זינתה, וקא אמר: "אי מהימנא לך דלאו גזלנא הוא זיל אפקה". והכא אי שתיק, מהימנא האשה:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:2.english: "And a woman says: He did not eat" - From here it is implied that a woman is believed more than a robber, for regarding a robber it is implied that we do not say silence is like an admission, as we say (Kiddushin 66a): "If he is trusted by you that he is not a robber, go divorce her," even though she was silent; thus we do not say silence is like an admission. And there was an incident: a certain blind man who used to recite baraitot before Rav Sheshet, etc., a certain man came and said that his wife had committed adultery, and [Rav Sheshet] said: "If he is trusted by you that he is not a robber, go divorce her." Yet here, if he is silent, the woman is believed.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:3.hebrew: עד אומר אכל והוא אומר לא אכלתי פטור - והוא הדין אם אמר "איני יודע", כמו שפירשתי:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:6:3.english: A witness says: He ate, and he says: I did not eat — he is exempt - And the same applies if he said, "I do not know," as I have explained.

Tosafot on Keritot 11b:9:1.hebrew: שאם אכל כחצי זית וחזר ואכל כחצי זית ממין אחד חייב משני מינין פטור - וא"ת: והא אמרינן בפ' קדשי מזבח (מעילה יז:): "הפיגול והנותר אין מצטרפין", וקא אמר בגמרא: "לא שנו אלא לטומאת ידים, אבל לאכילה מצטרפין"? וי"ל: דהתם לענין מלקות, אי נמי לענין שאם יפלו לקדירה אחת מצטרפין לתת טעם, דהא שם אחד הוא, דליכא אלא חד לאו אתרווייהו; אבל הכא מיירי לדין חיוב קרבן:
Tosafot on Keritot 11b:9:1.english: "[In a case] where one ate half an olive-bulk and then ate [another] half an olive-bulk, from one type he is liable; from two types he is exempt." - And if you ask: But we say in the chapter [entitled] Kodshei Mizbe'ach (Me'ilah 17b): "Piggul and notar do not combine," and the Gemara says: "They taught [this] only with regard to impurity of the hands, but with regard to eating they combine"! And one can answer: There it is with regard to lashes, or else with regard to [the case] where if they fall into one pot they combine to impart flavor, for it is one category, as there is only one negative commandment for both of them; whereas here it is speaking of the law of liability for an offering.
